title: We’re helping farmers around the world connect to essential services online.
body: We’re helping farmers around the world connect to essential services online. Rowan Barnett Director Google.org, APAC, EMEA & Global Stronger Communities Oct 26, 2026 Under the World Bank Group’s AgriConnect initiative, Google.org is supporting the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and broader World Bank Group (WBG) to better empower farmers . Their collective goal is to help 1 million farmers access crucial livelihood-improving services by the end of 2027. With Google.org’s $2.5 million in support, the WBG will expand digital public infrastructure (DPI) for agriculture: shared digital systems that act as “public roads” for online services. Following a successful pilot in India, the WBG will build an AI-enabled Open Network for Agriculture (ONA) across several countries spanning Latin America, Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. By connecting public and private sector service providers in a shared digital network, ONA lets farmers avoid separate, disconnected apps, using a single platform to access vital resources like digital farmer IDs, credit lines, direct subsidy payments, markets to sell produce, and voice-powered advice in their local language on farming, weather, pricing, and finances. This support builds on an alliance between Google and the World Bank Group to accelerate digital transformation in emerging markets.
retained_feed_body: Google.org is investing $2.5M to help 1 million farmers access AI-powered agricultural services via the World Bank's ONA. See how it works.

Where are HARD shares going? Access To China's Commodity Markets Without A K-1 The Simplify Chinese Commodities Strategy No K-1 ETF (NYSE: CCOM ) is designed to provide diversified long and short exposure to commodity futures traded on major Chinese exchanges, including those in Shanghai, Dalian and Zhengzhou. The fund uses a structure that bypasses the issuance of a Schedule K-1, a feature that may appeal to investors seeking simpler tax reporting. CCOM is built on a systematic long/short managed futures strategy developed by Altis Partners . The approach seeks long-term capital appreciation through investments in commodity-linked swaps and futures tied to more than 30 China-based commodity markets. By focusing specifically on contracts traded on Chinese exchanges, the fund aims to offer diversification benefits for portfolios heavily skewed toward U.S.-centric commodities. Simplify said China represents one of the world's largest and most influential commodity markets, yet many of its futures contracts remain difficult for U.S. investors to access directly. The firm positions CCOM as a way to tap into commodity exposures that may behave differently from traditional U.S.-based benchmarks, potentially enhancing diversification. The strategy combines two core models. A primary model analyzes price movements across multiple time horizons, while a secondary model is intended to help offset periods when trend-following strategies struggle. In addition, the fund dynamically manages futures curve positioning to account for contango and backwardation, factors that can materially impact returns in commodity markets. CCOM expands Simplify's existing lineup of commodity-focused ETFs. UNHW builds on strong investor demand for the WeeklyPay™ series by expanding the lineup into its first Health Care underlier, UnitedHealth Group. Following today's launch, the Roundhill WeeklyPay™ suite offers exposure to twenty different single stock underliers spanning across six sectors: AAPL, AMD, AMZN, ARM, AVGO, BABA, BRK/B, COIN, COST, GOOGL, HOOD, META, MSFT, MSTR, NFLX, NVDA, PLTR, TSLA, UBER, and UNH. The Fund will provide exposure to the weekly total returns of the stocks they track. Accordingly, the Fund is not an appropriate investment for investors seeking exposure to the daily total return of the stock they track. It is critical that investors understand the following: An investment in the Fund is not an investment in the underlying stock. Each Fund's strategy is subject to all potential losses of the tracked stock. If the tracked stock shares decrease in value, the Fund may lose all of its value if shares of the tracked stock decrease by 83.33 percent over the course of any calendar week. Issuer Specific Risks. Issuer-specific attributes may cause an investment held by the Fund to be more volatile than the market generally. The value of an individual security or particular type of security may be more volatile than the market as a whole and may perform differently from the value of the market as a whole. Derivatives Risk. Distribution Tax Risk. The Fund currently expects to make distributions on a weekly basis. Such frequent distributions may expose investors to increased tax liabilities. However, these distributions may exceed the Fund's income and gains for the Fund's taxable year. The Fund obtains investment exposure in excess of its net assets by utilizing leverage and may lose more money in market conditions that are adverse to its investment objective than a fund that does not utilize leverage. An investment in the Fund is exposed to the risk that a decline in the weekly performance of shares of the security indicated by the Fund's name will be magnified. Swap Agreements Risk. Swap agreements may involve greater risks than direct investment in securities as they may be leveraged and are subject to credit risk, counterparty risk and valuation risk. A swap agreement could result in losses if the underlying reference or asset does not perform as anticipated. In addition, many swaps trade over-the-counter and may be considered illiquid. It may not be possible for the Fund to liquidate a swap position at an advantageous time or price, which may result in significant losses. Concentration Risk. The Fund is susceptible to an increased risk of loss, including losses due to adverse events that affect the Fund's investments more than the market as a whole, to the extent that the Fund's investments are concentrated in investments that provide exposure to of the security indicated by the Fund's name and the industry to which it is assigned. Active Management Risk. The Fund is actively-managed and its performance reflects investment decisions that the Adviser and/or Sub-Adviser makes for the Fund. Such judgments about the Fund's investments may prove to be incorrect. If the investments selected and the strategies employed by the Fund fail to produce the intended results, the Fund could underperform as compared to other funds with similar investment objectives and/or strategies, or could have negative returns. New Fund Risk. The Fund is new and has a limited operating history. Non-Diversification Risk. title: Mayr-Melnhof Karton AG (WBO:MMK) (H1 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Fit-For-Future Program ...
body: Mayr-Melnhof Karton AG (WBO:MMK) (H1 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Fit-For-Future Program ... GuruFocus News August 20, 2026 6 min read MMK.VI MMK This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Sales: EUR1.85 billion, slightly down year-over-year on a like-for-like basis, but stable compared to the second half of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA: Approximately EUR200 million, significantly up compared to the second half of 2025. Adjusted Operating Profit: Close to EUR90 million, notably higher than the second half of 2025. EBITDA Margin: 10.8%, an increase compared to both the prior year and the second half of 2025. Operating Cash Flow: EUR145 million, significantly better than the prior year due to good working capital management. Capital Expenditure: Close to EUR112 million, stable to prior periods, including investments in the Kwidzyn ROE project. Net Debt: EUR945 million, below EUR1 billion. Net Debt-to-Adjusted EBITDA Ratio: 2.4, within the company's long-term target range of 2 to 2.5. Free Cash Flow: EUR37 million, a positive achievement for the first half of 2026. Equity Ratio: 47%, unchanged from year-end. Food & Premium Packaging Adjusted EBITDA Margin: Increased by 90 basis points year-over-year. Pharma Adjusted EBITDA Margin: Improved by almost 200 basis points, surpassing 14%. Board & Paper Price Deviation: Negative impact of approximately EUR70 million due to lower prices. Board & Paper Fit-For-Future Contribution: EUR59 million profit improvement, nearly offsetting the price decline. Capacity Utilization: Average of 87% for the Board & Paper division, with FBB specifically at 80%. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with WBO:MMK. Is WBO:MMK fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Release Date: August 20, 2026 For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript . Positive Points Strong performance in Pharma & Healthcare Packaging, with EBITDA margin improving by almost 200 basis points to surpass 14%. Fit-For-Future program delivering above expectations, with a projected earnings enhancement of over EUR330 million by 2027, up from the initial EUR250 million target. Successful market share gains in Europe for both recycled and virgin cartonboard, with over 90% of folding cartonboard sales now in Europe. Solid balance sheet with equity ratio at 47% and net debt-adjusted EBITDA ratio of 2.4, within the long-term target range. Strategic acquisition of Arnsberg mill from Reno de Medici, expected to generate substantial synergies and consolidate the market. Negative Points Lower pricing in Board & Paper division, with a price deviation of about EUR70 million, leading to a decline in profitability. Persistent overcapacity in the FBB (virgin cartonboard) market, with major competitors unwilling to shut down capacity, delaying price recovery. Higher transport and energy costs due to the Iran war, with transport costs up about 10% and energy costs expected to rise further in H2. Subdued consumer demand and ongoing price competition, particularly in the FBB segment, impacting overall results. Elevated capital expenditure levels in 2026 and 2027, mainly due to the Kwidzyn project, which will keep CapEx above the long-term maintenance level. Story Continues Q & A Highlights Q : Can you explain how the Fit-For-Future savings targets are calculated, and are they based on fixed or variable costs? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) explained that savings are only recognized after being in the books for at least one month, with some observed for three to six months to ensure sustainability. The program covers operations, procurement, top-line growth, SG&A, and supply chain. In procurement, improvements are measured against market indices, while in sales, surcharges and volume increases are counted only if they exceed market trends. The savings are more weighted toward variable costs than fixed costs, with the breakdown for H1 2026 being EUR27 million in Food & Premium Packaging, EUR16 million in Pharma & Healthcare, and EUR59 million in Board & Paper. Q : What is the rationale behind acquiring the Arnsberg mill from Reno de Medici, given the oversupplied market, and what are the investment needs and turnaround timeline? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) stated that the acquisition makes sense due to the proximity of Arnsberg to MM's Neuss mill, allowing for significant synergies in SG&A costs and maintenance. The mill produces WLC liner in lighter grammages. There are no significant investment needs, and the focus is on reducing costs, improving machine utilization, and specializing products across the combined asset base. The deal is signed but not yet closed, pending competition clearance. Q : What supports the expectation of improving prices in Board & Paper, and can you quantify the expected improvements by grade and region? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) differentiated between recycled cartonboard (WLC) and virgin cartonboard (FBB). For WLC, market closures in Spain, Holland, and Germany have brought the market closer to balance, leading to implemented price increases from April through July, with the trend expected to continue. For FBB, the market remains oversupplied due to two market leaders fighting for share, and no price improvement is predicted until capacity is shut down. Other grades like saturated kraft paper have good prices, while uncoated fine paper is weak but moving up. Q : Can you quantify the cost inflation across major cost positions (energy, wood, recycled fiber) and what is expected for the full year? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) noted that wood costs are marginally up, with regional variations (down in Scandinavia, up in Central Europe). Paper for recycling indices are gradually moving up. Chemicals are a mixed bag with no major impact. The main issues are transport costs, up about 10% due to the Iran war, and energy costs, which are expected to be higher in H2 than H1. The ability to pass on these costs depends on market balance; in oversupplied markets, passing on costs is difficult. Q : Is it fair to assume the Board & Paper division will be slightly positive on an adjusted basis in H2, given price increases, savings, and cost inflation? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) declined to give a precise forecast but indicated a stable development minus the annual maintenance costs of EUR35 million. The outcome depends on whether the EUR50-60 million Fit-For-Future contribution and other positives outweigh higher energy and transport costs. He noted high variance due to unpredictable gas prices, but suggested the result would be at a similar level minus the maintenance impact. Q : What is the target profitability level for the Pharma & Healthcare Packaging division, and how much more restructuring is needed? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) stated that the EBIT margin should be clearly above 10%, with some operations already in the 15% range. Restructuring is essentially complete, with possibly one small plant still under review. The main driver for margin improvement will shift to top-line growth, particularly from new products developed with pharmaceutical companies under long-term contracts, such as GLP-1 products, which have better margins. Q : How is Mayr-Melnhof positioned regarding gas hedging, and could higher gas prices force competitors to take economic downtime, benefiting MM? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) revealed that MM's gas hedging is somewhat below 50%, giving a slight advantage in the recycled business. However, in FBB, MM has a slight disadvantage as Frohnleiten is fully integrated but Kotka is only partly integrated, requiring more purchased energy. The investment in an e-boiler at Kotka will provide more flexibility. He noted that competitors like Volk (bankrupt) and Reno de Medici (bond restructuring) may be less able to hedge, potentially leading to more rational behavior or closures. Q : What visibility do you have on delivering the increased Fit-For-Future contribution of over EUR330 million by 2027? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) explained that the company tracks projects by "run rate" levels. Currently, about EUR270 million is at L4 (executed for at least one month and deemed sustainable), which is already banked. The L3 pipeline includes projects in testing or procurement phases, providing confidence that the EUR330 million target is conservative and likely to be upgraded again at the full-year results announcement. Q : What is the expected CapEx level for 2027, and what is the factoring level at the end of H1? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) clarified that long-term CapEx is EUR180-200 million per annum, including maintenance CapEx of EUR110-120 million. This year and next year are elevated due to the Kwidzyn projects, with 2027 CapEx expected to be roughly in line with this year or slightly down. Franz Hiesinger (CFO) added that net factoring was below EUR340 million, the same as at year-end 2025. Q : Regarding wood costs in Poland, are there any concerns about supply restrictions and inflation, and what lobbying efforts is MM undertaking? A : Peter Oswald (CEO) acknowledged lobbying efforts but noted that Poland has lost 30,000 jobs in the wood converting industry due to bankruptcies, which is adjusting demand to supply. Wood price increases in Poland are from a much lower base and are less severe than in Austria or other Central European countries, so the situation is not particularly worrying. Try Elite for Free Login Sign up free Home Stock Screener Screener ETF Screener ETF Maps Charts News Groups Insider Futures Forex Crypto Watchlist Portfolio Calendar Pricing Help New Upgrade: Dedicated Screeners for Stocks & ETFs Learn more Market News Market Pulse Stocks News ETF News Crypto News VanEck Targets India Growth Surge With New ETF As Investors Reassess Emerging Markets Exposure By Chandrima Sanyal | February 24, 2026, 3:38 PM DGIN +1.58% VanEck Digital India ETF GLIN +0.58% VanEck India Growth Leaders ETF INDZ +1.05% VanEck India Select ETF TRUC -0.15% VanEck Communication Services TruSector ETF TRUD +1.75% VanEck Consumer Discretionary TruSector ETF TRUT +1.11% VanEck Technology TruSector ETF As global investors revisit emerging markets allocations amid steady domestic growth signals from India and continued uncertainty around China, asset managers are refining how they offer exposure to the country's equity story. In that context, VanEck introduced two new ETFs last week: the VanEck India Select ETF (NYSE: INDZ ) and the VanEck Communications Services TruSector ETF (NASDAQ: TRUC ). The launches reflect two parallel themes shaping ETF demand: more selective country allocations and closer alignment between sector funds and benchmark construction. A More Selective Take On India India has increasingly stood out within emerging markets, supported by structural reforms, infrastructure investment, rapid digital adoption and favorable demographics. But the country's equity market is also marked by high dispersion, where company-level fundamentals can drive sharply different outcomes. VanEck is positioning INDZ as a strategy designed for that environment. Unlike traditional market-cap weighted India ETFs, the fund follows an actively managed, rules-based process that combines bottom-up research with quantitative screening. The focus, according to the firm, is on businesses demonstrating capital efficiency, resilient operating models and the potential for sustainable long-term earnings growth. The argument behind the structure is straightforward: broad benchmarks may dilute returns by allocating capital across companies with widely varying quality profiles. By concentrating on firms seen as consistent value creators, the ETF aims to reduce what the firm characterizes as structural drag from persistent underperformers. INDZ expands VanEck's existing India suite, which includes the VanEck Digital India ETF (NYSE: DGIN ), focused on companies linked to the country's digitalization theme, and the VanEck India Growth Leaders ETF (NYSE: GLIN ), which targets fundamentally strong firms with growth characteristics. With INDZ, the firm appears to be targeting investors looking for a more selective core allocation rather than thematic or pure growth exposure. Rethinking Sector Construction Alongside its India expansion, VanEck is also extending its TruSector ETF framework into communications services through TRUC. The TruSector lineup, which already includes the VanEck Consumer Discretionary TruSector ETF (NASDAQ: TRUD ) and the VanEck Technology TruSector ETF (NASDAQ: TRUT ), is designed to address what the firm views as a structural limitation in traditional sector ETFs. Under Registered Investment Company (RIC) diversification rules, funds may be required to cap exposure to large constituents. This might lead to underweights to dominant stocks and heavier allocations to smaller names. VanEck's approach uses a hybrid structure that combines direct equity holdings with targeted ETF exposure. The goal is to maintain uncapped sector representation while remaining compliant with RIC rules, thereby reducing tracking error relative to widely followed benchmarks. With market performance increasingly driven by a narrow group of mega-cap stocks and sector concentration becoming more pronounced, the firm appears to be positioning TRUC as a more precise way to express a communications services view. (Nasdaq: KOYN) and First Digital Group Ltd. Announce A Letter of Intent for a Proposed Business Combination to Create a Global Stablecoin and Digital Payments Leader By CSLM Digital Asset Acquisition Corp lll Ltd | December 02, 2025, 6:30 AM KOYN +0.15% CSLM Digital Asset Acquisition Corp III Ltd First Digital Group is a leading stablecoin and digital asset infrastructure provider, and the group behind FDUSD - the #3 most-traded stablecoin globally - supported by a compliance-first, fully backed trust framework and a rapidly expanding global payments and infrastructure ecosystem NEW YORK and HONG KONG, Dec.  02, 2025  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- First Digital Group Ltd. (“First Digital” or the "company") and CSLM Digital Asset Acquisition Corp III, Ltd. (“KOYN”), a publicly listed special purpose acquisition company, jointly announce that they have entered into a non-binding letter of intent (“LOI”) for a proposed business combination. Upon completion, the combined company is expected to be publicly listed on a national securities exchange in the United States. First Digital Group: A Global Leader in Digital Asset Infrastructure First Digital has established itself as one of the most progressive and fastest-growing innovators in digital finance, evolving from its roots in traditional trust and custody services into a global provider of institution-ready digital asset infrastructure. Founded in 2019 and restructured under Gibraltar-based First Digital Group Ltd. in 2022, the company now operates across multiple jurisdictions with a compliance-first operating model and a proven record of delivering secure, reliable, and scalable financial technology solutions. At the center of First Digital's offering is FDUSD, a USD-denominated stablecoin fully backed by cash and cash equivalents held in a Hong Kong-registered, bankruptcy-remote trust structure. FDUSD has rapidly established itself as one of the most actively traded stablecoins on centralized exchanges, reaching more than US$1 billion in market capitalization within its first four months and later surpassing a peak circulation of more than US$4.4 billion as adoption accelerated. Supported by tier-1 exchange integrations and world-class liquidity partners, FDUSD has processed more than US$2 trillion in cumulative trading volume since launch, demonstrating deep liquidity and sustained demand across global markets. Fully backed by segregated reserves held with its licensed custodian affiliate and supported by independent monthly attestations and robust AML/KYC controls, FDUSD has become a trusted and scalable digital dollar for exchanges, institutional users, and on-chain payment applications. First Digital operates a compliance-first regulated foundation with licenses, and registrations, in key financial centers. The company's rapidly expanding product ecosystem includes stablecoin-as-a-service solutions for corporates, global stablecoin payment rails with real-time settlement capabilities, on-chain and off-chain APIs for commerce, swap services, custody, minting/redemption, and merchant tools, as well as infrastructure enabling cross-border settlement, remittances, and DeFi integrations. The company currently expects to report approximately US$80-$90 million in unaudited revenue for 2025, reinforcing its position as a leading force in the transition toward the modern digital asset economy. First Digital are ready to launch Finance District - a decentralized finance ecosystem built on a foundation of institutional trust, which will mark a major milestone for First Digital. At its core is Prism, an agentic payments and settlement layer that allows autonomous AI agents and digital assistants to transact, settle, and distribute value at machine speed using FDUSD. This unlocks an entirely new category of AI-powered finance—enabling businesses to automate revenue flows, streamline operational costs, and participate in a rapidly expanding on-chain economy without compromising compliance or reliability. With Finance District, First Digital is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of DeFi, where programmable payments, community governance, and real-world utility converge to create the financial infrastructure of the autonomous economy. For additional information about First Digital, please visit: https://1stdigital.com/ir-and-disclosures Separately, First Digital had filed a writ of summons on April 3, 2025, in the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Court of First Instance initiating a defamation action against Sun Yuchen (a/k/a Justin Sun) in response to his public allegations. Additional information and publicly available filings regarding this matter can be found at: https://1stdigital.com/ir-and-disclosures Strategic Rationale for the Proposed Business Combination KOYN's management team has deep experience across SPAC transactions, digital assets, and structured capital markets, and believes First Digital is uniquely positioned to become a global leader in a sector benefiting from intensifying global regulatory clarity for stablecoins; explosive growth in cross-border payments, remittances, and on-chain settlement; increasing institutional demand for fully backed, compliant, transparent stablecoins; and the shift toward Web3 payments infrastructure and programmable money. The combined company aims to accelerate First Digital's international scaling, broaden its product suite, and further institutionalize its regulatory and compliance footprint. Management Commentary First Digital Founder & CEO Vincent Chok: Taking the world’s first APAC-rooted and emerging-market-focused USD stablecoin issuer public is a milestone not just for First Digital, but for the evolution of digital finance globally. We have spent years building the infrastructure of trust. Transparent reserves, regulated structures, and institution-ready rails, and today marks the beginning of the next chapter. With the launch of the Finance District and our agentic payments layer, Prism, later this year we are opening the door to real-time, AI-powered settlement and a new generation of programmable commerce. This proposed combination with KOYN positions us to scale globally and continue shaping the future of trusted digital dollars.” CSLM Digital Asset Acquisition Corp III, Ltd Chairman Vik Mittal: "We are humbled to partner with a visionary of Vincent's standing. Custody, integrity and trust. Programmable money collapses the world’s payment networks into one global dollar network. We’re finally rewriting the world’s financial rails from scratch. It’s been a long time coming." Definitive Documentation The parties will announce additional details regarding the proposed business combination when a definitive agreement is executed. No assurances can be provided as to the entry into or timing of any definitive agreement or the consummation of any transaction. Any transaction would be subject to the completion of satisfactory due diligence, the negotiation of a definitive agreement and related ancillary agreements providing for the proposed business combination, satisfaction of the conditions negotiated therein, board and shareholder approvals, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. Advisors Cohen & Company Capital Markets is serving as exclusive capital markets and M&A advisor to First Digital. Loeb & Loeb LLP is serving as legal counsel to KOYN. DLA Piper LLP (US) and DLA Piper UK LLP are serving as legal counsel to First Digital. Additional Information and Where to Find It If a definitive agreement is entered into in connection with the proposed business combination, the company or a newly formed holding company will prepare and file a proxy statement/prospectus with the SEC. KOYN urges investors and securityholders to read the proxy statement/prospectus and other documents filed with the SEC when they become available, as they will contain important information regarding the proposed business combination. The proxy statement will be distributed to holders of KOYN’s Class A Ordinary Shares in connection with KOYN’s solicitation of proxies for the vote by KOYN’s shareholders with respect to the proposed business combination and other matters as will described therein. All SEC filings will be available free of charge at www.sec.gov. Participants in the Solicitation KOYN, First Digital, and their respective directors, officers, and employees may be deemed participants under SEC rules in the solicitation of proxies in connection with the proposed business combination. Information about KOYN’s directors and officers is available in KOYN’s SEC filings. Additional details regarding the interests of persons involved in the proposed business combination will be included in the proxy statement/prospectus when it becomes available. About First Digital Group Ltd. First Digital is a leading digital asset and stablecoin infrastructure provider, offering fully backed USD-denominated stablecoins, trust and custody services, global payment solutions, and white-label stablecoin issuance for enterprises. Its flagship product, FDUSD, is one of the world’s most traded stablecoins, supported by a compliance-first governance model, segregated trust structure, and monthly independent attestations. First Digital operates across multiple jurisdictions and maintains active licenses and registrations in key financial centers. About CSLM Digital Asset Acquisition Corp III, Ltd. KOYN is a publicly traded special purpose acquisition company focused on high-growth, frontier-technology sectors including digital assets, regulated financial infrastructure, and next-generation fintech. KOYN is led by an experienced SPAC team with a track record of sourcing, executing, and stewarding complex public-market transactions. SAN FRANCISCO , Jan. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bitwise Asset Management, the global crypto asset manager with over $15 billion in client assets, in partnership with Proficio Capital Partners, an investment advisory firm with $5 billion in client assets serving high-net-worth families and foundations, today announced the launch of the Bitwise Proficio Currency Debasement ETF (NYSE: BPRO). BPRO follows an actively managed investment strategy targeting assets poised to benefit from the declining purchasing power of fiat currencies, including bitcoin , gold, silver, precious metals, and mining equities. The fund will adjust exposures as market conditions change, ensuring the portfolio is guided by Bitwise's specialty in digital assets and Proficio's longstanding expertise in precious metals. "For decades, investors have relied on a simple mix of stocks and bonds to protect their wealth, but that traditional playbook is struggling in an era of rapid monetary expansion," said Matt Hougan, Chief Investment Officer at Bitwise. "By combining the historical scarcity of gold with the modern, digital scarcity of bitcoin , BPRO offers a powerful new way to hedge against the persistent decline of fiat currency. We believe this 'hard asset' approach is the missing piece for the modern portfolio." Over the past two decades, the U.S. dollar has lost roughly 40% of its purchasing power, with the national debt climbing from $7.5 trillion to $38 trillion. In a recent Bitwise/VettaFi survey, financial advisors cited fiat debasement as one of the most important themes to watch in 2026, with 22% of advisors citing that as a critical area of focus. 1 BPRO provides a strategic response to these well-founded concerns. "Despite its stellar performance, gold remains a ghost in the modern portfolio. According to Goldman Sachs, gold ETFs account for just 0.17% of private financial holdings, meaning the asset is still remarkably under-owned," said Bob Haber, CIO at Proficio. "Currency debasement isn't just a theoretical risk; it is an active tax on every dollar an investor saves. BPRO represents the evolution of our wealth preservation mission, shifting between precious metals and digital stores of value to help provide a flexible shield as the purchasing power of global currencies continues to erode." The Fund seeks capital appreciation by investing in assets that may benefit from currency debasement. The Fund will target a minimum of 25% in gold at any point, and will strategically allocate across other assets such as silver, platinum, palladium, and other related equities, along with bitcoin . The Fund combines Bitwise's deep crypto expertise with Proficio Capital Partners' extensive experience investing in specialized precious metals. Founded in 2014 by Matthew Wosk and Bob Haber, Proficio is a $5 billion investment advisory firm that has spent the last 12 years refining the currency debasement strategy on which BPRO is based. Today, the firm provides sophisticated wealth management solutions to a diverse client base of high-net-worth families, businesses, and foundations. The Bitwise Proficio Currency Debasement ETF is now trading on NYSE under the ticker BPRO. It has a total expense ratio of 0.96%. About Bitwise Bitwise Asset Management is a global crypto asset manager with more than $15 billion in client assets and a suite of over 40 crypto investment products spanning ETFs, separately managed accounts, private funds, hedge fund strategies, and staking. The firm has an eight-year track record and today serves more than 5,000 private wealth teams, RIAs, family offices, and institutional investors, as well as 21 banks and broker-dealers. The Bitwise team of over 140 technology and investment professionals is backed by leading institutional investors and has offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. About Proficio Capital Partners Founded in 2014 by Matthew Wosk and Bob Haber, Proficio Capital Partners is a Boston-based investment advisory firm, headquartered in Newton, MA, dedicated to providing discretionary services to high-net-worth families, individuals, and foundations. Originally established as a private family office, the firm has expanded to serve a diverse institutional clientele, including private funds and insurance-dedicated investment vehicles. Under the investment direction of Bob Haber, CFA—former CIO of Fidelity Investments Canada and a Lipper Award-winning Portfolio Manager—Proficio leverages institutional expertise to deliver bespoke wealth management solutions. As of December 31, 2025, the firm manages approximately $5 billion in assets. The Fund is nondiversified and will not invest in crypto assets directly or through the use of derivatives and also will not invest in initial coin offerings. The Fund may, however, have indirect exposure to crypto assets by virtue of its investments in Crypto ETPs that use one or more crypto assets as part of their business activities or that hold crypto assets as proprietary investments. Investors in the Fund should be willing to accept a high degree of volatility in the price of the Fund's shares and the possibility of significant losses. title: How Google Beam connects military families globally
body: How Google Beam connects military families globally Oct 26, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Together with the USO, we are bringing Google Beam to 20 locations globally so deployed service members can experience lifelike, 3D video connections with their loved ones. Watch our new docuseries to see how four military families are staying connected, despite being miles apart. Josh Woodward VP, Google Labs, Gemini, & AI Studio Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Google is partnering with the USO to bring HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 locations worldwide. This 3D video technology helps deployed service members feel truly present with their families by capturing lifelike body language and eye contact. You can watch the new docuseries to see how this tool bridges the distance for military families and visit the Google Beam website to learn more. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. "How Google Beam connects military families globally" shows how tech bridges the distance for soldiers. Google is partnering with the USO to bring 3D video communication to 20 locations. This lifelike technology helps families share milestones, like first steps and promotions, in real time. It captures body language and eye contact, making long-distance chats feel much more personal. You can watch a new docuseries to see how these reunions impact military families. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Google Beam uses AI to create lifelike 3D video calls that make it feel like you’re sitting right across from someone. Google is partnering with the USO to bring this tech to military families stationed far apart. It helps soldiers stay connected to their loved ones by capturing real-time body language and eye contact. This makes missing big moments, like a child’s first steps, feel a lot less lonely. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer For deployed service members, the hardest distance is measured in missed moments. A child’s first steps, a first performance, or simply sitting across the table from a loved one feels out of reach. That's why we’re partnering with the USO to bring HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 USO locations globally, helping service members bridge this distance. With Beam’s unique true-to-life, 3D video communication experience, families feel like they’re stepping into the same room and connecting in a whole new way. Google Beam began a pilot program connecting families between Trzebień, Poland, and Fort Bliss, Texas earlier this year. Now, we’re releasing a docuseries that shows how the program is expanding to Grafenwöhr, Germany, and Fort Hood, Texas, bringing this lifelike closeness to even more families. Directed by military veteran and filmmaker Kyle Hausmann-Stokes, our new docuseries captures the power of this connection. It follows four soldiers from the 2nd Battalion, 37th Armored Regiment (Iron Dukes) during their deployment in Poland. Watch the profound emotional impact of Google Beam as they reconnect with their families back home, proving that love knows no distance. Four families, one shared mission The Brown-Orane family Sergeant Amoy Brown is a Bradley Gunner deployed in Poland, and Tiyanna Orane, his wife, is an aviation logistics specialist in Fort Bliss. For them, military service is an equal partnership. But an eight-hour time difference makes celebrating major milestones,like Tiyanna’s military promotion, feel distant. Google Beam helped create an intimate, lifelike reunion where Amoy and Tiyanna could celebrate her achievement, and Amoy could interact with their young son, Azeal. The Kassales family Throughout his first two years of service, Army Chaplain Roland Kassales has been deployed for 15 months. Staying present with this family during the time apart is incredibly important. Google Beam helped bridge the distance, bringing his family into focus. When his daughter, Blythe, read stories she wrote to him aloud, Beam let him experience those moments in real time with the body language, eye contact, and all. The Jennings family Mayra Jennings manages a bustling, blended household of seven while working 12-hour work shifts, leaving her deployed husband, Sergeant First Class Matthew Jennings, feeling the absence of daily family life. Standard phone calls made it difficult to connect across the miles with their 4-year-old son, Dimitri, their newborn daughter, Lilly, and his two sisters. Google Beam gave Matthew a front-row seat to experience how much his newborn daughter had grown, to see one of his sisters play guitar, and offered Mayra a moment of comfort, recreating the feeling and warmth of sitting directly across the table from one another. The Rodriguez family Major Michael Rodriguez, an armor battalion operations officer with 12 years of service, knows the heavy toll deployments take, especially on his family. His wife Jessica balances a demanding job as a pediatric physical therapist, while solo parenting their four young children. With Google Beam they’re able to create new memories, including witnessing his one-year-old daughter Kathryn practice taking her first steps. Watch the docuseries To see these emotional reunions and follow the journey of the Brown, Kassales, Jennings, and Rodriguez families, watch the complete docuseries . And to learn more about how Beam is redefining human connection visit goo.gle/USO . title: National Crime Victimization Survey Shows Violent Crime Plummeted in 2025
body: Press Release National Crime Victimization Survey Shows Violent Crime Plummeted in 2025 Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Non-fatal violent crime dropped 25% from 2024 to 2025 New preliminary estimates from the Bureau of Justice Statistics’ (BJS) National Crime Victimization Survey (NCVS) show that the rate of violent crime, property victimization, burglary or trespassing, motor vehicle theft, and other types of household theft fell significantly in 2025. “This report is proof that President Trump’s ‘Make America Safe Again’ agenda is working,” said Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward. “Under President Trump and Attorney General Blanche, the safety of law-abiding Americans will always come first. This success reinforces our commitment to ensuring every American can live, work, and raise a family without fear.” According to the survey, the rate of non-fatal violent crime excluding simple assault declined 25% from 9.9 per 1,000 persons age 12 or older in 2024 to 7.4 per 1,000 in 2025. Violent crime excluding simple assault, also known as serious violent victimization, includes the crimes of rape or sexual assault, robbery, and aggravated assault. The rate of aggravated assault also declined 31% from 2024 (4.5 per 1,000 persons age 12 or older) to 2025 (3.1 per 1,000). The rate of property victimization declined 19% from 138.0 per 1,000 households in 2024 to 111.2 per 1,000 in 2025. Further, the rates of burglary or trespassing (down 25%), motor vehicle theft (down 30%), and other types of household theft (down 19%) decreased from 2024 to 2025. The NCVS is the nation’s primary source of information on criminal victimization, including crimes reported and not reported to police. Each year, BJS collects information from a nationally representative sample of about 240,000 persons, aged 12 or older, in about 150,000 U.S. households on the frequency, characteristics, and consequences of non-fatal criminal victimization in the United States. BJS fully transitioned to the redesigned National Crime Victimization Survey (NCVS-R) instrument in January 2025. This report presents the inaugural estimates from the fully transitioned NCVS-R. For more information on the 2025 preliminary estimates, visit Preliminary Findings from the NCVS, 2025 . These results follow last week’s publication of the BJS report, Homicide Victimization in the United States, 2025 , which showed homicide rates fell 17% in 2025 over 2024. Updated October 26, 2026 Component Office of the Associate Attorney General Press Release Number: 26-1260

title: Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 48 Aliens for Election Related Crimes
body: Press Release Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 48 Aliens for Election Related Crimes Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the Justice Department announced charges involving 48 aliens in Pennsylvania, California, Florida, New York, and Nevada in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration, and related election crimes. The cases include voting by aliens in federal elections and false claims of U.S. citizenship to register to vote or to vote. Case details are as follows: Eastern District of Pennsylvania Four aliens, including an illegal alien, have been charged with illegally voting. Alfredo Santiesteban, 73, an illegal alien from Cuba, has been charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. Santiesteban allegedly voted in the 2024 general election. Polish national Artur Kopacz, 50, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with two counts of voting by an alien. Kopacz allegedly voted in the 2022 and 2024 general elections. Cuban national Osmal Loy, 70, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. Loy allegedly voted in the 2024 general election. Cuban national Osmal Loy, 70, a lawful permanent resident Israeli national Yehuda Peer, 30, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. Peer allegedly voted in the 2024 general election. Israeli national Yehuda Peer, 30, a lawful permanent resident Middle District of Pennsylvania Five aliens have been charged with illegally voting. Kenyan national Nina Nyawara, 21, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien. Nyawara allegedly voted in an election held for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, U.S. Senator, and Member of the House of Representatives in 2024. Russian national Inna Henry, 52, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien. Henry allegedly voted in an election held for the purpose of electing a candidate for U.S. Senator and Member of the House of Representatives in 2022. Russian national Inna Henry, 52, a lawful permanent resident Kenyan national Joyce Donovan, 38, a lawful permanent resident, with voting by an alien. Donovan allegedly voted in an election held for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, U.S. Senator and Member of the House of Representatives in 2024. Dutch national Joyce Pitts, 80, a lawful permanent resident, with voting by an alien. Pitts allegedly voted in an election held for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, U.S. Senator and Member of the House of Representatives in 2022. Dutch national Joyce Pitts, 80, a lawful permanent resident Greek national Nourten Kuruju, 64, a lawful permanent resident, with voting by an alien. Kuruju allegedly voted in an election held for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, U.S. Senator and Member of the House of Representatives in 2022. Central District of California The following 13 defendants in this jurisdiction face felony charges, including false statements in a naturalization application. Belizean national Omar Alexander Muñoz, 72, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in September 2019, claiming he was a U.S. citizen, then voted in U.S. elections in 2020, twice in 2022, and in 2024. He also lied in his application to become a naturalized U.S. citizen when he falsely stated under oath that he had never claimed to be a U.S. citizen. Belizean national Omar Alexander Muñoz, 72, a lawful permanent resident Indian national Amandeep Kaur, 30, a lawful permanent resident, who is seeking to become a U.S. citizen, allegedly registered to vote in December 2022 and voted in the November 2024 U.S. election. Salvadoran national Ana Domínguez, 60, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in July 2006 and lied in her naturalization paperwork in March 2026. Salvadoran national Ana Domínguez, 60, a lawful permanent resident Guatemalan national Axel Giovani Prera García, 46, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2002 and 2005, and lied in his naturalization paperwork in June 2025. Maxican national Flavio Alejandro Zúñiga, 43, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2003 and lied in his naturalization paperwork in February 2026. Cambodian national Butleng Taing, 43, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in July 2021, voted in the 2022 and 2024 U.S. elections, and lied in his naturalization paperwork in August 2025. Cambodian national Butleng Taing, 43, a lawful permanent resident Honduran national Carlos Antonio Galeas, 54, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2012 and 2016, then lied in his naturalization paperwork in September 2018. Honduran national Carlos Antonio Galeas, 54, a lawful permanent resident Mexican national Ernest Gutiérrez Ruvalcaba, 57, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in February 2024 and voted one month later. Mexican national Jesús Narez-Madrigal, 52, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2014, voted in the 2024 U.S. general election, and lied in his naturalization paperwork in June 2024. Mexican national Jesús Narez-Madrigal, 52, a lawful permanent resident Mexican national José Antonio Bañuelos-Díaz, 42, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2007 and lied in his naturalization paperwork in March 2025. Pakistani national Muhammad Khan, 50, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly submitted a provisional ballot in 2020 and lied in his naturalization paperwork five years later. Canadian national Rouzbeh Seyamaknejad, 63, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in December 2018, lied in his naturalization application in January 2024, and voted in the November 2024 U.S. election. Canadian national Rouzbeh Seyamaknejad, 63, a lawful permanent resident Mexican national Sulema de León, 35, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2013, lied in her naturalization application in 2019, and voted in the November 2020 U.S. general election. Eastern District of California The following six defendants have been charged with voting by an alien in a federal election, a misdemeanor that carries a statutory maximum sentence of one year in federal prison. Mexican national Maricela Nazarín González, 43, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2020, indicating that she was a U.S. citizen, and voted in elections in 2022, twice in 2024, and 2025. Mexican national Maricela Nazarín González, 43, a lawful permanent resident Guatemalan national Rony de Jesús Sicaja, 38, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2017, and voted in the June 2022 primary election and the 2024 general election in the United States. Mexican national Camino Giles Jiménez, 51, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly voted in three U.S. elections despite knowing he is a noncitizen, the most recent election being the June 2026 primary. Mexican national Juan Antonio Rivas García, 46, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2018 and 2020, both times falsely asserting under oath that he was a U.S. citizen. Rivas voted in the 2022 and 2024 U.S. elections. Filipino national Giezell Viduya Adawag, 41, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote the day of the November 2024 general election, falsely certified that she was a U.S. citizen, and voted in the election that day. Filipino national Giezell Viduya Adawag, 41, a lawful permanent resident Indian national Kamlesh Navnitlal Shah, 67, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote on the day of the November 2024 general election and voted that day. He is charged by information. Northern District of California The following five defendants have been charged with attempted procurement of naturalization contrary to law, false statement under oath in any matter relating to naturalization or citizenship, and voting by an alien. Mexican national Verónica Bullene, 43, a.k.a. “Verónica Hernández Martínez”, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly made false statements in her naturalization application that she had never claimed to be a U.S. citizen when, in fact, she did so under penalty of perjury to register to vote in 2022 and 2023 then voted in 2024. Georgian national David Shapiro, 41, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2024 and later voted in a U.S. election, and made false statements in his naturalization application that he had never claimed to be a U.S. citizen. Myanmar national Moe Thida Lwin, 57, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in 2024 and then proceeded to illegally vote in a U.S. citizen. She made false statements in her naturalization paperwork as well. Tongan national Manakotau Mataele Finau, 61, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote in the 2024 election, voted, and then lied about it in naturalization paperwork. Ecuadoran national Maribel del Carmen Garcés Barriga, 62, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly made false statements in her naturalization paperwork that she  had never claimed U.S. citizenship and had never voted in a U.S. election or had registered to vote. In fact, Garcés fraudulently registered to vote in 2024 and proceeded to vote in a U.S. election. Southern District of California The following four defendants have been charged with false claim to citizenship to vote, unlawful attempted procurement of naturalization, and false statement under oath in matter relating to naturalization or citizenship. Filipino national José Probitsado Amaro, 51, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. He then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements during his naturalization interview, denying that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting his voting history. Filipino national José Probitsado Amaro, 51, a lawful permanent resident Canadian national Jennifer Jung, 31, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. She then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements during her naturalization interview, denying that she had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting her voting history. Guatemalan national Erick Ronaldo Soto Mendizábal, 64, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. He then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements in his naturalization application, denying that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting his voting history. Filipino national Pamele Arbués Line, 56, a lawful permanent resident, allegedly voted in the November 2024 general election, and made false statements in her naturalization interview, denying that she had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting her voting history. Filipino national Pamele Arbués Line, 56, a lawful permanent resident Middle District of Florida Six aliens have been charged with election related crimes. Cuban national Jamie Orlando Sosa Sardina, 60, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by indictment with making a false statement claiming U.S. citizenship to vote and illegal voting by an alien. Sardina allegedly registered to vote in 2022 and voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections. Cuban national Jamie Orlando Sosa Sardina, 60, a lawful permanent resident Ecuadorian national Martha Haydee Desantis, 81, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by indictment with making a false statement claiming U.S. citizenship to vote and illegal voting by an alien. Desantis allegedly re-registered to vote in 2024 and voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections. Canadian national Lise Marie Johnson, 69, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by indictment with making a false statement claiming U.S. citizenship to vote and illegal voting by an alien. Johnson allegedly registered to vote in 2021 and voted in the 2022 federal general election. Canadian national Lise Marie Johnson, 69, a lawful permanent resident Cuban national Luis Manuel Perez, 72, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with illegal voting by an alien. Perez allegedly voted in the 2022 and 2024 federal general elections. Cuban national Luis Manuel Perez, 72, a lawful permanent resident Canadian national Diane Wendy Curley, 55, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with illegal voting by an alien. Franco, 37, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with illegal voting by an alien. Franco voted in the 2024 federal general election. Northern District of New York German national Marva Cook, 66, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien. Cook allegedly voted in an election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives. German national Marva Cook, 66, a lawful permanent resident Eastern District of New York Three aliens have been charged with election related crimes. Irish national Eoin Cranney, 35, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with voting by an alien in a federal election. Cranney allegedly submitted a fraudulent voter registration application and voted in the 2024 federal general election.  In a voluntary interview with federal agents, Cranney admitted, in substance and in part, that he was not a U.S. citizen, that he had registered to vote in 2024, and that he had voted in the 2024 federal general election knowing that he was not a U.S. citizen. title: Fort Walton Beach Man Pleads Guilty to Federal Drug Trafficking & Firearm Offenses
body: Press Release Fort Walton Beach Man Pleads Guilty to Federal Drug Trafficking & Firearm Offenses Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – Anthony Bernard Allen, 54, of Fort Walton Beach, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to two counts of possession with intent to distribute cocaine, as well as possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Our state and federal law enforcement partners are relentlessly pursuing the armed drug traffickers who have plagued our communities with deadly drugs and violence for far too long, and my office is backing up their efforts with successful prosecutions like this one. My message to the peddlers of drugs in this district is clear: your days are numbered, and a federal prison cell is in your future.” Court documents reflect that on March 19, 2026, law enforcement executed a search warrant at the defendant’s Fort Walton Beach residence, where officers seized 950 grams of cocaine, 37 grams of cocaine base, a loaded handgun, and ammunition. The defendant is a convicted felon who cannot legally possess a firearm or ammunition. Less than one month later, on April 17, 2026, the defendant was the subject of a traffic stop where officers observed him attempting to discard a bag of cocaine onto the ground. Allen faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 5 years in prison, and up to 40 years’ imprisonment, followed by up to a lifetime of supervised release. The case was investigated by the Okaloosa County Sheriff’s Office, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Drug Enforcement Administration with assistance from the Gulf Coast High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas (HIDTA) Task Force. Assistant United States Attorney Brooke D. Lindsay is prosecuting the case. Allen’s sentencing is scheduled for December 29, 2026, at 1:00 p.m., at the United States Courthouse in Pensacola before United States District Judge T. Kent Wetherell, II. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. title: Tallahassee Man Pleads Guilty to Attempted Enticement of a Minor
body: Press Release Tallahassee Man Pleads Guilty to Attempted Enticement of a Minor Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – Brandon Garrett Ursrey, 46, of Tallahassee, Florida has pleaded guilty in federal court in Tallahassee on one count of attempted enticement of a minor. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida, announced the guilty plea. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Our state and federal law enforcement partners are committed to keeping our kids safe online and in our communities, and thanks to their relentless pursuit of predators who seek to sexually exploit and victimize children through the internet we have been able to successfully prosecute this defendant. My office will continue to aggressively prosecute these cases to ensure we keep these sick individuals locked behind bars and away from our kids.” Court records reflect that in November 2025, a multi-agency undercover operation was conducted to identify adults who use the internet to sexually exploit children. During the operation, the defendant contacted an undercover officer, who he believed to be a 15-year-old child, and engaged in sexually explicit conversation over a two-day period. The defendant made arrangements to meet at a Tallahassee apartment complex that he believed was the 15-year-old’s residence in order to engage in sexual activity with the child. The defendant was arrested upon his arrival at the apartment complex.  After his arrest, forensic analysis of the defendant’s phone verified he was the one communicating with the undercover investigator. Ursrey faces a minimum mandatory ten years up to life imprisonment and is scheduled for sentencing in federal court before Chief United States District Judge Allen C. Winsor on January 22, 2027, at 10:00 a.m. in Tallahassee, Florida. This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, the Tallahassee Police Department, and St. John’s County (Florida) Sheriff’s Office. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric K Mountin. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General.  To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . body:
Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises: lending conditions tightened Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date PRESS RELEASE Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises: lending conditions tightened 26 October 2026 Firms reported a further net tightening of bank loan interest rates and other loan conditions related to price and non-price factors. Bank loan availability declined by more than financing needs, widening the financing gap. In this survey round the sample composition changed substantially, with first-time respondents accounting for the majority of the sample. This makes it more challenging to interpret the responses to the numerical questions – such as those on expectations for selling prices, input costs and inflation – at this stage. In the most recent round of the Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises (SAFE) in the euro area, covering the third quarter of 2026, euro area firms widely reported a further net increase in interest rates on bank loans (net 46%, compared with 42% in the previous quarter). Large firms reported increases more often (net 55%, up from 41%) than small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) (net 38%, down from 43%). At the same time, a net 27% of firms (down from 31% in the previous quarter) reported increases in other financing costs (i.e. charges, fees and commissions) and in collateral requirements (net 14%, up from 10%) (Chart 1). In this survey round, firms reported that the availability of bank loans had declined by more than their needs. Firms reported a decrease in the availability of bank loans in the third quarter of 2026 (-5%, compared with a net -1% in the second quarter of 2026), with both SMEs (net -5%, compared with -4%) and large firms (net -6%, down from 4%) reporting lower availability. At the same time, a net 2% of firms reported a decrease in their bank loan needs, while a net 2% reported an increase in the previous quarter. Developments in needs differed by firm size: SMEs reported broadly unchanged needs (net 1%, compared with 2%), while large firms reported a decrease (net -6%, down from 3%). As a result, the bank loan financing gap indicator, which captures the difference between changes in the need for and the availability of bank loans, was positive (net 2%, compared with 3% in the previous quarter) (Chart 2). Looking ahead, more firms expect the availability of external financing to decrease over the next three months. Firms continued to perceive the general economic outlook as the main factor constraining the availability of external financing (net 31%, compared with 29% in the previous survey round), with large firms now more pessimistic than SMEs (net 35% and 29%, respectively). In this survey round, a net 9% of firms indicated that their firm-specific outlook, in terms of sales and profits, had a negative impact on the availability of external financing (after 10% in the previous survey round), while the impact of their capital position and creditworthiness remained positive. The substantial change in the sample composition in this survey round, with first-time respondents accounting for the majority of the sample, makes it challenging to interpret the responses to the numerical questions at this stage. The increase in selling price expectations was contained among firms that took part in both this round and the previous one, whereas selling price expectations rose significantly in the full sample (Chart 3). Similarly, firms’ median inflation expectations remained broadly unchanged among firms that took part in both the current and previous survey rounds, whereas they rose significantly in the full sample (Chart 4). The risk assessment for firms’ five-year-ahead inflation outlook was broadly unchanged. The report published today presents the main results of the 40th round of the SAFE for the euro area. The survey was conducted between 26 August and 2 October 2026. In this survey round, around half of the firms were asked about changes in the period between July and September 2026. The remainder were asked about changes in the period between April and September 2026. Additionally, firms reported their expectations for euro area inflation, selling prices and other costs. The sample comprised 12,822 enterprises in the euro area, of which 11,917 (93%) had fewer than 250 employees. For media queries, please contact: William Lelieveldt , tel.: +49 170 227 9090. Notes The report on this round of the SAFE, together with the questionnaire and methodological information , is available on the ECB’s website . Detailed data series for the individual euro area countries and aggregate euro area results are available in the ECB Data Portal . Chart 1 Changes in the terms and conditions of bank financing for euro area firms (net percentages of respondents) Base: Firms that had applied for bank loans (including subsidised bank loans), credit lines, or bank or credit card overdrafts. The figures refer to rounds 33 to 40 of the survey (October-December 2024 to July-September 2026). Notes: Net percentages are the difference between the percentage of firms that reported an increase for a given factor and the percentage that reported a decrease. The data included in the chart refer to Question 10 of the survey. Chart 2 Changes in euro area firms’ financing needs and the availability of bank loans (net percentages of respondents) Base: Firms for which the instrument in question is relevant (i.e. they have used it or have considered using it). Respondents who replied “not applicable” or “don’t know” were excluded. The figures refer to rounds 33 to 40 of the survey (October-December 2024 to July-September 2026). Notes: The financing gap indicator combines both financing needs and the availability of bank loans at firm level. The indicator of the perceived change in the financing gap takes a value of 1 (-1) if the need increases (decreases) and availability decreases (increases). If firms perceive only a one-sided increase (decrease) in the financing gap, the variable is assigned a value of 0.5 (-0.5). A positive value for the indicator points to a widening of the financing gap. Values are multiplied by 100 to obtain weighted net balances in percentages. The data included in the chart refer to Question 5 and Question 9 of the survey. Chart 3 Expectations for selling prices, wages, input costs and employees one year ahead (percentage changes over the next 12 months) Base: All firms. The figures refer to rounds 30 to 40 (March 2024 to September 2026) of the survey, with firms’ replies collected in the last month of the respective survey waves. Notes: Mean and median euro area firm expectations of changes in selling prices, wages of current employees, non-labour input costs and number of employees for the next 12 months, along with interquartile ranges, using survey weights. Yellow squares denote the mean expectations of firms interviewed in both the Q2 and Q3 waves of 2026. The statistics are computed after trimming the data at the country-specific 1st and 99th percentiles. The data included in the chart refer to Question 34 of the survey. Chart 4 Firms’ median expectations for euro area inflation at different horizons (annual percentages) Base: All firms. The figures refer to rounds 31 to 40 (June 2024 to September 2026) of the survey, with firms’ replies collected in the last month of the respective survey waves. Notes: Survey-weighted median, mode and interquartile ranges of firms’ expectations for euro area inflation in one year, three years and five years. Quantiles are computed by linear interpolation of the mid-distribution function. Yellow diamonds denote the median expectations of firms interviewed in both the Q2 and Q3 waves of 2026. The statistics are computed after trimming the data at the country-specific 1st and 99th percentiles. The data included in the chart refer to Question 31 of the survey.
