title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
body: Politics Ukraine With repeat attacks, Russia has put Kyiv on war's front line Maryna Asmolova 10/23/2026 October 23, 2026 Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like. https://p.dw.com/p/5OaIc Russian attacks have turn Ukraine's capital into a front-line city Image: Marina Asmolowa/DW Advertisement Until a few months ago, life was relatively peaceful in Kyiv when compared with the situation near the war's front lines elsewhere in Ukraine . Now, as Russia expands its attacks on the capital, Kyiv has increasingly become a front-line city. With too few shelters for the 4 million residents of Kyiv , subway stations double as makeshift dormitories. Starting at about 10 every night, people create sleeping areas with mattresses and small tents. Children snuggle up to adults; pets seek comfort from their owners or find a spot among strangers between the cold walls. "We're alive," Halyna told DW, holding her 5-year-old son, Roman, close. "We've been lucky once again." Most evenings — even when no air-raid siren has sounded — she takes the boy to the nearest subway station. Her apartment is located in the Lukyanivka district, which Russia has systematically targeted over the war's four years and eight months. People lie on mattresses in the capital's subway system during the night Image: Marina Asmolowa/DW 'These sick monsters don't care who they kill' In September, 14-year-old Daniel Umanskyj was doing homework in his room when a Russian drone struck the apartment building in the central district of Pechersk. A neighbor named Vlad happened to be in the hallway with his daughter at the time of the strike. "We were late that day — and this saved our lives," Vlad said. "Daniel's death is a tragedy." He added: "These sick monsters don't care who they kill." Flowers have been planted in front of the damaged apartment building in memory of Daniel. Russia also targets places where children gather. In early October, a drone struck a school building  in southwestern Kyiv. Fortunately, pupils and teachers were already in shelters at the time. "We've been teaching all the pupils in person because we have a large shelter that can accommodate more than 500 students," Valentyna Chorna, the school's principal, told DW. As there is enough space in the shelter for everyone, students in the first through ninth grades are able to go to school, she said. 14-year-old Daniel was killed when an attack hit his building in Kyiv Image: Marina Asmolowa/DW Danger at home, at school — everywhere Whether classes take place depends not only on the decision of the parents and the school administration: It also depends on whether shelters are available and how long the air-raid siren continues to sound. If an alarm sounds in the morning while children are still at home, they may not be able to go to school that day. "This is an enormous burden for parents," said a colleague from the DW bureau in Kyiv, whose daughter attends school. "You have to go to work — and the child stays home alone." "Even the walk to school is dangerous because an air-raid alarm can go off at any time," she said. Her daughter attends a school not far from the Antonov aircraft factory. "One day she texted me: ‘You can't imagine what a huge explosion that was!'" she said. "I don't know if something was shot down or if there was a strike somewhere." She added: "Things like that really scare children." And staying home brings its own risks. In September, a Russian drone struck their building. The apartment itself wasn't damaged, and her daughter was at school that morning, but it was another reminder of just how much survival has become a matter of luck. When an air-raid siren sounds, no one knows who will be spared, she said. Attacks on Kyiv target civilian infrastructure, schools and places where children spend free time Image: Marina Asmolowa/DW Kyiv's population persists Russia's attacks have become deadlier in 2026. According to the military administration in Kyiv, 140 people were killed in the capital during the first eight months of the year, compared with 172 for all of 2025. If this trend continues, 2026 could become Kyiv's deadliest year since the start of the Russian invasion in 2022. Attacks on warehouses have led to shortages in supermarkets on a scale not seen since the early months of the war. At the end of September, emergency power outages resumed in Kyiv. The subway was paralyzed by a Russian attack. Given the strikes on the energy infrastructure, it is unclear how the capital can reliably supply residents with heat, electricity and water during the upcoming winter. Despite Russia's attempts to render Kyiv uninhabitable, 72% of the city's residents said in September that they are prepared to endure the war for as long as necessary, the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology reported in early October. The authorities are striving to maintain normal life in the city, where the curfew has been shortened and now runs from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. Some facilities have even been allowed to continue operating during "yellow" alerts. During "red" alerts, however, people must immediately seek shelter: This  could mean ballistic missiles, cruise missiles or massive combined attacks. Russia strikes Ukraine with massive aerial attack To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video This article was originally written in Ukrainian. title: Trump administration sues to block certification of upcoming Alaska election
body: Trump administration sues to block certification of upcoming Alaska election Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Senator Dan Sullivan, right, is in a tight race with Democratic contender Mary Peltola. By Bernd Debusmann Jr White House reporter Published 23 October 2026 The Trump administration wants to block the certification of the Senate election in Alaska if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses, arguing that another candidate with the same name may confuse voters. The justice department said in a federal lawsuit filed on Thursday that the inclusion of another Dan Sullivan on the ballot could lead some to mistakenly cast their votes for the wrong candidate. Polls suggest the race between Senator Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola is tight, with Peltola holding a narrow lead in the final days before the 3 November vote. The US government wants the judge to bar the state from certifying the results if Senator Sullivan loses by a margin less than the other Sullivan. "I'm the one that said do it," US President Donald Trump told reporters when asked for his thoughts on the lawsuit after he landed in Florida for a campaign rally on Friday. Trump has referred to the second Sullivan's candidacy as a "scam" and said his administration was looking at "powerful legal options" to end it. The retired teacher previously denied his candidacy had an ulterior motive. Previous efforts to remove that Sullivan, a retired teacher, from the ballot have already been rejected by the Alaska Supreme Court. For the 3 November midterm election, the senator will be listed on the ballot as the Republican incumbent. Alaska's ranked-choice voting system means that voters could select both Sullivans if they are unsure at the ballot box. In court documents, the justice department said Alaska "will fail in its obligation to protect the integrity of its elections" if it includes "any electoral results tainted by the inclusion on the ballot of Daniel J Sullivan". The second Sullivan, who was also a US Forest Service worker, was reportedly once a member of the Alaska Independence Party before registering as a Republican earlier this year. In the filing, Associate Attorney General Stanley E Woodward Jr asserted that the sole purpose of his candidacy was to benefit Peltola's campaign by reducing the number of votes for the senator. "Given the substantial likelihood that the inclusion of Dan J Sullivan will confuse or mislead voters looking to cast a vote for Senator Sullivan and thus distort the will of Alaskan voters, there is a substantial likelihood that a certification of the election will reflect an electoral process that lacked integrity," Woodward argued. Dan J Sullivan has repeatedly denied those claims, telling the local Petersburg Pilot newspaper earlier this year that he "wouldn't even know who to speak to" in Peltola's campaign. He said separately to Courthouse News that it was his "sincere hope that people know who and what they are voting for but, ultimately, choice is good and voters' intent will be as varied as the candidates who are running". In the event Peltola wins, and the margin of loss suggests possible confusion, the lawsuit calls for certification to be delayed pending an investigation into whether voters were mixed up on the names as well as any "necessary and appropriate" steps to determine what would have happened had the second Sullivan been kept off the ballot. Neither candidate has so far commented on the lawsuit. The Senate race in Alaska - which Trump won by 14 percentage points in 2024 - is among the most closely watched in the upcoming midterm elections. The president's approval ratings in the state have been badly hit by voter disapproval of rising prices and the war in Iran. GUIDE: What are the US midterms? EXPLAINED: Why Trump's approval rating matters in the midterms IN DEPTH: The Republicans walking a Trump tightrope Related topics US midterm elections 2026 United States US politics United States Senate Alaska

title: Treasury Issues Proposed Rule to Implement Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act
body: October 22, 2026 WASHINGTON– The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) today issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to propose updates to the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) based on direction from Congress in the Comprehensive Outbound Investment Security (COINS) Act, passed as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.  The COINS Act codifies the U.S. Government’s approach to regulating certain outbound investments by U.S. persons and builds upon Treasury’s existing OISP. In passing the COINS Act, Congress made clear that restricting certain U.S. outbound investments into dual-use strategic technologies that benefit a foreign adversary’s military modernization efforts, surveillance states, and human rights abuses is necessary to prevent harm to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. President Trump is committed to protecting our national security and the implementation of the COINS Act is consistent with maintaining a strong, open investment environment that benefits our economy and supports our national security interests. The COINS Act directs the Secretary of the Treasury (the Secretary) to issue regulations that (1) require United States persons to provide notification to Treasury regarding certain transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies, and (2) prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies.  The COINS Act authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations with technical parameters for “prohibited technology” and “notifiable technology” in five technology sectors: semiconductor technologies and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.  The COINS Act also authorizes the Secretary—in consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and subject to notice and comment rulemaking—to add and define technologies beyond those specifically listed in the law that enable the military, intelligence, surveillance, or cyber-enabled capabilities of a country of concern.  Accordingly, the Secretary has added biotechnology to the proposed regulations. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are committed to putting America’s national security first,” said Secretary Scott Bessent .  “The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security.  This important step also helps promote our commitment to an open investment environment by providing clarity to U.S. and foreign investors as well as an opportunity for them to provide feedback on the proposed regulations.” “The proposed regulations are designed to address risks that can arise when foreign adversaries try to benefit from U.S. investment in key technology sectors,” said Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security Christopher Pilkerton.  Pilkerton added, “It will enhance the Outbound Investment Security Program and our efforts to protect U.S. national security.” The NPRM issued today provides details on key concepts and aspects of the program’s proposed implementation, including: Requirements applicable to a U.S. person (including any controlled foreign entities); Categories of covered national security transactions; Definitions; The scope of covered foreign persons; Excepted transactions; Technical specifications to inform the scope of covered national security transactions based on certain technologies and products in the areas of semiconductor technology and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, super intelligence systems, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and supercomputing, and biotechnology; Information that a U.S. person is required to provide to Treasury as part of a notification; The process of requesting non-binding feedback and submitting confidential information; The knowledge standard and expectations for a U.S. person to conduct a reasonable and diligent inquiry prior to undertaking a transaction; and Conduct that would be treated as a violation of the proposed rule and applicable penalties for such conduct. Treasury invites comments from a wide range of stakeholders on all aspects of the NPRM including feedback on the scope of a covered national security transaction, definitions of key terms, the notification requirements, and the penalty and enforcement processes for violations, among other aspects.  Treasury will carefully consider this input before issuing the final implementing regulations. Written comments may be submitted by the deadline in the official NPRM, available at https://www.regulations.gov .  The NPRM will be followed at a later date by final implementing regulations, which will set an effective date for the program. The NPRM, fact sheet, and additional information are available at: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/outbound-investment-program .

title: The Trump Administration is Making Homeownership More Affordable
body: October 22, 2026 Proposed Rules Implement the ROAD to Housing Act and Support Affordable Homeownership in America WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury issued proposed regulations to make homeownership more affordable for hardworking Americans. The proposed regulations implement Section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (ROAD to Housing Act), which restricts large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, codifying key requirements of President Trump’s Executive Order 14376 , Stopping Wall Street from Competing with Main Street Homebuyers . “Under President Trump, this Administration continues to restore the path to affordable homeownership for millions of young and working families,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Treasury is working to ensure American families and workers have a fair shot at purchasing homes in their communities by increasing housing supply and limiting large institutional investors’ role in the market, while supporting a strong, stable housing market and avoiding unnecessary disruption.” RESTORING THE AMERICAN DREAM OF HOMEOWNERSHIP Beginning on January 7, 2027, a large institutional investor generally may not purchase, or enter into a contract to purchase, a single-family home unless the purchase qualifies as an “excepted purchase” under the ROAD to Housing Act. The ROAD to Housing Act defines a large institutional investor by reference to, among other things, whether an entity is engaged in the business of investing in, owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes and has direct or indirect investment control over at least 350 such homes. The ROAD to Housing Act permits several categories of excepted purchases, including purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs, renovate-to-rent programs, homeownership programs, and programs to boost homeownership. Today’s NPRM sets forth Treasury’s proposed framework to: Establish standards for purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs that promote continued investment in new housing; Provide a safe harbor for purchases made pursuant to renovate-to-rent programs that bring neglected homes back into the housing supply and up to code; Clarify the requirements for homeownership programs and programs to boost homeownership, including providing safe harbors for large institutional investors that provide meaningful financial support towards their renters’ purchase of a home; Clarify that an entity is engaged “in the business of” investing in , owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes when it does so for the purpose of receiving income or financial gain, and not incidentally to a different business; Define when an entity may qualify as a passive investor in another entity that owns a home because it does not share directors or officers with the other entity and does not have a property control right over the underlying homes; Clarify certain purchases involving debts previously contracted, loss mitigation, and transfers between large institutional investors that protect the liquidity of the housing market; and Clarify the calculation of the maximum civil penalty where a single prohibited purchase involves more than one large institutional investor. The proposed rule would provide non-exclusive safe harbors for several statutory requirements. These include standards for determining whether a home has been substantially rehabilitated under a renovate-to-rent program, whether a renter has received meaningful financial support under certain homeownership programs, and whether a renter has received a right of first refusal and 30-day first-look period. Treasury’s proposed approach recognizes that housing-market participants use a variety of ownership, investment, construction, servicing, and property-management structures and seeks to provide clarity without unnecessary disruption to housing supply, homebuilding, rehabilitation activity, or capital formation. Members of the public should submit comments in response to the NPRM within 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. The proposed regulations are available here . ###

title: October 22, 2026 - FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus to coordinate agency action on brain and nervous system conditions, with inaugural focus on Alzheimer's prevention For Immediate Release: October 22, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced the launch of the Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus (NAIN) , a new agency program aligned with the Trump Administration’s efforts to accelerate medical innovation and deliver breakthrough treatments. NAIN is designed to advance the science, tools, and regulatory approaches needed to support the development of medical products for conditions affecting the brain and nervous system. NAIN’s inaugural initiative, the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator , will focus on advancing medical products that help delay or prevent Alzheimer's disease. Both efforts support the National Alzheimer’s Project Act (NAPA), the federal government's comprehensive roadmap for coordinated action on Alzheimer's and related dementias. "The launch of NAIN reflects FDA's commitment — in support of the Trump Administration’s drive to transform health care innovation — to making sure our regulatory science and cross-center collaboration keep pace with the rapid advances happening in neuroscience," said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. "Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, we are bringing the full breadth of FDA's expertise to bear on one of the most urgent public health challenges of our time.” Developing medical products for neuroscience indications is associated with complex scientific and clinical challenges, including limited understanding of underlying biology, variable disease presentation, and difficulties in demonstrating meaningful clinical benefit, particularly for conditions that develop over many years. Advances in biomarkers, digital health technologies, and other medical product development tools, however, offer important opportunities to address these challenges. NAIN will bring together scientific and regulatory expertise from the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and Center for Devices and Radiological Health to address scientific and regulatory questions that benefit from coordinated consideration across drugs, biologics, and devices. NAIN will encompass conditions that affect the brain and nervous system broadly, including neurologic and psychiatric disorders, substance use disorders, and pain. NAIN will also support robust engagement with patients, industry, academia and other stakeholders to advance these efforts. As its first initiative, NAIN is launching the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator . This inaugural initiative will draw on perspectives from across the FDA and engage patients and caregivers, researchers, industry, public-private partnerships and other government agencies. The initiative will explore innovative approaches to advancing clinical trials for Alzheimer’s disease prevention and early-intervention drug development with emphasis on trial populations, stage-appropriate endpoints, and evidentiary approaches for demonstrating prevention or delay of cognitive decline due to Alzheimer’s disease. The FDA has long been committed to supporting the development of safe and effective medical products that address diseases and conditions of the brain and nervous system. Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, the agency is taking a proactive, coordinated approach to accelerating progress, bringing together its scientific and regulatory expertise, engaging the broader research and development community, and working in concert with federal partners to meet the scale of this public health challenge. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Shadow Fleet Networks
body: October 21, 2026 Law Firms, Shipping Agents, and Vessels Helped Conceal and Transport Iranian Commodities WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctioned Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis , which has supported illicit Iranian shipping activity for years, indirectly aiding Tehran’s ability to generate revenue to fund its military, weapons, and nuclear programs.  Throughout Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury has continued to coordinate with counterparts in Europe and around the world to sever the Iranian regime’s remaining economic lifelines. “Whether you are conducting illegal oil transfers at sea or sitting in the corner office of a law firm, if you are supporting the Iranian regime, we will find you and sanction you,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Iran’s facilitators must make a choice: Either you are with us or against us. We know who you are, we know what you’re doing, and we will continue to take action.” Treasury today also sanctioned Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents that directly aid Iranian shadow fleet operations.  Today’s actions strike not only the legal and maritime facilitators that sustain Iran's sanctions-evasion networks, but also a fleet of cargo vessels that has helped generate substantial revenue for the Iranian regime. The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum and petrochemical sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. FinCEN is acting in close coordination with European partners, including in Greece, and leveraging existing legal authorities, such as its first issuance of an administrative subpoena pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 5318(k) of the Bank Secrecy Act, to advance its investigation into a Greek bank’s potential ties to Iran and its proxies. Additionally, FinCEN has issued multiple requests for information concerning banks’ relationships with OFAC-designated Iranian financial institutions. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026 and dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime. Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system.  Operation Economic Outcast also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . LAW FIRM ESTABLISHING SHADOW FLEET ARCHITECTURE Through Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury is targeting law firms and corporate service providers that establish shell and front companies for persons trading in sanctioned Iranian products, an essential service needed for any such malign actor to evade sanctions or regulatory compliance.  Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis has for years leveraged its legal practice to register shipping companies that own shadow fleet vessels responsible for shipping hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian steel, petroleum, and petrochemicals, among other goods.  The firm previously set up the companies Skyros Maritime and Trading S.A. , Corfu Maritime and Trading S.A. , and Elias Shipping and Trading Group S.A. , among others, all of which OFAC has previously designated for their ownership of vessels active in the trade of Iranian petroleum and petroleum products. Elias Shipping and Trading SA, the owner of the RAMONA 1 (IMO: 9233222), served as a front company for the Al-Qatirji Company, a Syrian firm responsible for selling millions of barrels of Iranian oil for the benefit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF) and Houthis.  The Al-Qatirji Company at the time of its designation was one of the main financial channels for the IRGC-QF, enabling the terrorist group to generate and access hundreds of millions of dollars a year in revenue gained from the sale of Iranian oil. Karnakis and Karnakis played a particularly critical role in establishing the corporate architecture for the shipping empire of Iranian liquified petroleum gas (LPG) magnate Seyed Asadoollah Emamjomeh (Emamjomeh), which is collectively responsible for shipping hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian LPG and crude oil.  Karnakis and Karnakis served as the corporate agent for many of Emamjomeh’s firms, including several that were ultimately designated for their role in shipping Iranian petroleum products. Karnakis and Karnakis was founded, and is currently owned, by dual Panamanian-Greek nationals Sofianos Karnakis Kosmas and Konstantinos Karnakis Kosmas , with Panamanian-Greek national Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas and Panamanian national Pedro Ortega Jones serving as employees of the law firm.  Karnakis and Karnakis employees, including Panamanian national Roberto Ortega Jones , act as directors and officers of many of the companies they register in order to obfuscate the true beneficial owners of these companies. Karnakis and Karnakis is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum and petrochemical sectors of the Iranian economy.  Sofianos Karnakis Kosmas, Konstantinos Karnakis Kosmas, Pedro Ortega Jones, Roberto Ortega Jones, and Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Karnakis and Karnakis. CARGO FLEET VESSELS Iran relies on seemingly legitimate cargo vessels to move Iranian petrochemicals and other products, including steel.  Panama- and Greece-based Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. (Roxette), for which Karnakis and Karnakis serves as the corporate agent, is the operator and ship manager of the Panama-flagged vessels ANEMOS (IMO 9205952), GLORIS (IMO 9449510), and PRIDE (IMO 9487407), all of which have shipped various cargos of Iranian-origin goods within the past year, including petrochemicals and steel products.  In addition, Roxette is the ship manager and operator of the Panama-flagged cargo vessels DESTINY (IMO 9385491), FLAMINGO 1 (IMO 9474199), HARMONY (IMO 9449522), and PRINCE (IMO 9548316). Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petrochemical sector of the Iranian economy.  ANEMOS, GLORIS, PRIDE, DESTINY, FLAMINGO 1, HARMONY, and PRINCE are being identified pursuant to E.O. 13902 as blocked property in which Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. has an interest. SHIPPING AGENTS AIDING SHADOW FLEET Shipping agents play a critical role in shadow fleet operations by aiding the transit of illicit Iranian cargo through ports, including oil, petroleum, and other commodities.  Treasury is taking action against two shipping agents that have helped Iran transport its products to buyers around the world. Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. (Amigoz) is a Singapore-based full-range shipping agency that provides port agency services.  Amigoz acted as the agent for a shipment of light crude oil overseen by Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company, which oversees a network of front companies that supports the allocation of billions of dollars’ worth of commodities to Iranian military entities.  As of 2026, Amigoz has been associated with a range of dark fleet actors, including some affiliated with the shipping empire of Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani , and provided bunkering services to the Iranian shadow fleet vessel ZIXUAN (IMO 9317298). Whales Shipping Line LLC (Whales), a Dubai-based maritime and logistics company, acted as the shipping agent for Sparrow Trading FZE, a sanctioned Dubai-based front company that organized the purchase of tens of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian petrochemicals in coordination with Persian Gulf Petrochemical Industry Commercial Co.  Whales has also conducted business worth hundreds of thousands of dollars with Amigoz.  Whales is the registered owner of two UAE-flagged small support vessels: WHALES DIAMOND (IMO 9375032) and WHALES PEARL (IMO 9483114). Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy.  Whales Shipping Line LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd.  WHALES DIAMOND and WHALES PEARL are being identified as blocked property in which Whales Shipping Line LLC has an interest. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . Click here for more information on the persons designated today . ###

title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Issues Final Guidance on Prescription Drug Apps and Software
body: FDA News Release FDA Issues Final Guidance on Prescription Drug Apps and Software New policy clarifies when app content requires FDA review and how drug-connected software must be described on medication labels For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today released final guidance establishing a clear framework for how drug companies can develop, distribute, and label apps used alongside their prescription medicines. The guidance ends longstanding uncertainty by providing recommendations about when app content is subject to FDA submission requirements, when an app should be mentioned on a drug’s official label, and what companies should submit to the agency. “Mobile apps are playing a growing role in how patients manage their medications and health conditions,” said Captain Chris Wheeler, Pharm.D., Director of the Division of Medical Policy Programs within FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “This guidance helps ensure that the information these tools provide is accurate, evidence-based, and clearly communicated to both patients and their providers.” The guidance addresses three key questions for industry: when app content is treated as FDA-required labeling versus promotional labeling, when an app should be referenced in a drug’s official prescribing information, and what companies should submit to FDA when they distribute app content to users. The guidance identifies two categories of companion software: Apps connected to a medical device (such as an app paired with an asthma inhaler) generally should be described on the drug’s official prescribing label, given the central role the software plays in how the medicine is used. Standalone apps (such as symptom trackers, dose reminders, or health coaching tools) should appear on the prescribing label if the company can show the app is essential for safe and effective use or can demonstrate a meaningful clinical benefit. In most cases, content a companion app displays to users will be treated as promotional material, consistent with how the FDA handles other drug advertising. “This guidance reflects FDA’s commitment to responsible, risk-proportionate oversight of digital health, an area that is a key priority for the agency and is evolving rapidly and holds significant promise for improving patient care,” said Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., Director of the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “By aligning our approach across drug and device centers, we are giving developers a clear and consistent pathway to bring safe, effective digital health technologies to patients.” “Companion apps are quickly moving beyond simple dose reminders toward tools that adapt to each patient,” said Jared Seehafer, M.S., FDA Deputy Commissioner for Technology . “Finalizing this guidance gives drug companies and their technology partners a stable foundation to build on as these technologies advance and helps ensure patients and providers can trust the information they receive.” This guidance also reflects the FDA’s ongoing commitment to modernizing its regulatory framework to keep pace with rapidly evolving digital health technologies. By providing clear, practical recommendations for both drug-connected software and standalone software, the agency aims to reduce unnecessary uncertainty for developers and manufacturers while preserving the safety and effectiveness standards that patients and healthcare providers rely on. The final guidance is available here . title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration yesterday approved the first generic of Climara Pro (estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system, 0.045 mg per day/0.015 mg), a transdermal hormone therapy patch for women with an intact uterus applied once a week. The approval aligns with FDA’s Public Health Pillar : Increasing Access to Affordable Medicines & Medical Products. “Menopause is a universal experience for women, and it can greatly affect a person’s quality of life. This approval makes effective treatment more accessible,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “Approvals like this reflect FDA’s ongoing commitment to expanding American patient access to safe, affordable, high-quality medications.” The generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system is therapeutically equivalent to Climara Pro, which is indicated for use in women with an intact uterus for: Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause Prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system contain both estrogen and progestogen in a single patch; this differs from estrogen-only patches commonly used in menopause treatment. Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system are specifically approved for women with an intact uterus, as the progestogen component is included to reduce the risk of endometrial hyperplasia that can occur with estrogen use alone. “Once-weekly dosing can make a real difference in how patients manage their care,” said Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., Director of FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “A patch offers a convenient alternative to daily oral medications, which may help patients stay on track with their treatment.” Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system are contraindicated in patients with undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; breast cancer or a history of breast cancer; estrogen-dependent neoplasia; active deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE) or a history of these conditions; active arterial thromboembolic disease or a history of these conditions; known anaphylactic reaction or angioedema or hypersensitivity to estradiol and levonorgestrel; hepatic impairment or disease; and protein C, protein S, or antithrombin deficiency, or other thrombophilic disorders. The most common adverse reactions (greater than or equal to 5%) are: application site reaction, vaginal bleeding, breast pain, upper respiratory infection, back pain, depression, pain, headache and flu syndrome. In the U.S., nine out of 10 prescriptions filled are for generic drugs. Increasing the availability of generic drugs helps to create competition in the marketplace, which then helps to make treatment more affordable and increases access to healthcare for more patients. Learn more about the FDA Drug Competition Action Plan . Climara Pro is a registered trademark of Bayer. The FDA approved Zydus Pharmaceuticals (USA) Inc.’s Estradiol and Levonorgestrel Transdermal System. Please contact the manufacturer for information about the medicine’s availability. title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment New treatment may allow some patients to maintain viral control after stopping all hepatitis B therapy For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection, in combination with existing antiviral therapy, to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in certain adults without cirrhosis. Hibsago is the first FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide to treat chronic hepatitis B. Hibsago is approved for certain adults without cirrhosis who have been taking HBV antiviral therapy for at least six months, have suppressed levels of HBV in their blood and have hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less, as determined by an FDA-authorized test. “For many people living with chronic hepatitis B, treatment can mean taking antiviral medication for years to keep the virus suppressed,” said Wendy Carter, DO, Acting Director of the Office of Infectious Diseases in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Hibsago provides a new treatment approach that gives some patients the possibility of maintaining control of the virus after all chronic HBV treatment has ended. This approval represents an important advance for people living with this serious disease.” Chronic hepatitis B is a long-term liver infection caused by HBV. Over time, the infection can lead to serious liver disease, including cirrhosis, and increase the risk of liver cancer. Hibsago works by targeting the genetic instructions the virus uses to make copies of itself and viral proteins, helping reduce the amount of virus and hepatitis B surface antigen in the body. The FDA also authorized the Roche Elecsys HBsAg II quant II RxDx assay as a companion diagnostic device to aid in the selection of patients with chronic HBV infection for treatment with antiviral therapy in accordance with the FDA approved drug labeling and to assist in monitoring patients throughout the course of treatment. Researchers studied Hibsago in two clinical trials that compared it with a placebo, an inactive treatment. Hibsago is injected under the skin for up to 24 weeks. Patients take it alongside their existing hepatitis B medicine and continue that medicine for at least 24 weeks after their last Hibsago injection. Some patients may then be able to stop their existing medicine if they meet certain health and lab test requirements. Across the two trials, 24% of patients who received Hibsago met the requirements to stop their existing medicine, compared with none who received placebo. Twenty-four weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment, 19% of patients who received Hibsago still had the virus under control, and a protein that signals hepatitis B infection (HBsAg) could not be detected in their blood. Hibsago has a boxed warning for serious liver reactions as well as low platelet counts, which can increase the risk of potentially life-threatening bleeding. Hibsago also has warnings for worsening kidney function, serious inflammatory adverse reactions like vasculitis, and serious risks if the injection is not administered properly. Patients need regular blood tests and follow up with their healthcare provider before and during treatment to monitor these risks. The most common side effects, excluding laboratory abnormalities, are injection site reactions, fever, fatigue and headache. The FDA granted Hibsago Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations as well as Priority Review . The approval was granted to GSK plc. title: National Republican Senatorial Committee v. Federal Election Comm’n
U.S. Treasury Identifies $270 Million in Suspicious Activity Linked to Federal Student Aid Fraud
body: October 19, 2026 FinCEN Refers Findings to Federal Investigators to Combat Fraud and Protect Taxpayer Dollars WASHINGTON - The U.S. Department of the Treasury announced today that its Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has identified approximately $270 million in suspicious financial activity potentially linked to fraud against federal student aid programs. FinCEN has referred these findings to federal investigators to pursue potential fraud schemes targeting federal student aid programs and help ensure those responsible are held accountable. These referrals underscore the Trump Administration’s commitment to eliminating fraud, protecting taxpayers, and safeguarding the integrity of federal student aid programs. “Federal student aid is intended to expand educational opportunities, not line the pockets of fraudsters who steal from students pursuing their education and hardworking taxpayers,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “The Trump Administration will not tolerate criminals who exploit government programs for personal gain. Treasury is working with financial institutions and law enforcement to identify these fraud schemes, recover stolen funds, and hold those responsible accountable.” “Federal student aid is meant to support students, not fraudsters. That is exactly why we introduced the new FAFSA fraud detection tool earlier this year, which stops fraud at the start of the federal student aid process,” said Education Secretary Linda McMahon. “We are proud to partner with the White House Task Force to combat fraud, waste, and abuse across these critical programs – already saving American taxpayers more than $2 billion in less than 2 years!” In a July 2026 Alert , FinCEN warned financial institutions about student aid fraud and asked them to report suspicious activity. That Alert explained that schools or their payment contractors often send aid refunds by electronic bank transfer and that the payment description often includes the word “refund” along with the school’s name or initials. The Alert also noted that fraudsters often move stolen aid through money mules, shell companies, and fake accounts to hide the source of the money. These red flags help financial institutions spot suspicious payments and report them to FinCEN in suspicious activity reports, as required by the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA). Financial institutions have filed nearly 100 suspicious activity reports since the July Alert. FinCEN’s review of these reports identified more than 20,000 potentially suspicious transactions since February 2026. These reports reflect suspicious activity that has been identified and reported by financial institutions and, therefore, should not be considered a complete representation of the scope of any particular type of suspicious activity.  Accordingly, FinCEN has referred this information to law enforcement as tip-and-lead information for further investigation. Federal student aid fraud schemes often involve fraudulent enrollments designed to divert financial assistance away from legitimate students. In “ghost student” schemes, criminals steal personal information, such as names and Social Security numbers, and use it to enroll fake students in classes under a victim’s identity. Fraudsters may also use super intelligence to produce fake documents that blend stolen information with invented details, which creates what are known as synthetic identities that can pass identity checks. Victims, including minors, often do not know that someone has received student aid in their name. In “straw student” schemes, fraud rings pay real people for their personal information, enroll those people at a school, and then keep the aid refunds issued to them. Corrupt school employees sometimes help these rings by recruiting straw students and altering their school records. Student aid fraud drains taxpayer funds, and in some cases, keeps real students out of classes that fake enrollees have filled. Student aid fraud has real consequences for students and American taxpayers. It drains finite grant resources from deserving students, potentially prevents legitimate students from enrolling in classes occupied by fraudulent enrollees, and can leave identity theft victims responsible for debts they never incurred. As part of the Trump Administration’s efforts to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse across the federal government, Treasury is working with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, led by Vice President Vance, and encouraging whistleblowers to report credible information involving fraud, money laundering, sanctions violations, and tax-law violations. Whistleblower tips, combined with financial institutions’ reporting under the Bank Secrecy Act, help Treasury and its law enforcement partners uncover criminal networks, recover taxpayer funds, and hold bad actors accountable. Treasury will continue to leverage financial intelligence, strengthen coordination across government, and pursue those who seek to profit by defrauding American taxpayers and harming legitimate students. ###

title: October 19, 2026 - FDA Approves Immunotherapy That May Allow Certain Patients with Rectal Cancer to Avoid Chemotherapy, Radiation and Surgery
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves Immunotherapy That May Allow Certain Patients with Rectal Cancer to Avoid Chemotherapy, Radiation and Surgery For Immediate Release: October 19, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for a new use of the immunotherapy Jemperli (dostarlimab-gxly) that may allow some patients with locally advanced rectal cancer to avoid common treatments that can have a lasting impact on their daily life. Patients with locally advanced rectal cancer often receive chemotherapy and radiation prior to surgery, which can affect bowel, urinary, and sexual function, as well as fertility. Surgery also carries risks of serious, sometimes life-threatening complications, including poor healing and leaks where the bowel is reconnected, and in some patients, permanent colostomy. “The FDA is committed to closing the gap between scientific progress and patient access, and that commitment has to show up not just in policy, but in the pace of our work,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “American patients deserve timely access to innovative treatments, and the Trump Administration is making that a reality. Completing this review nearly 4 months ahead of schedule means some patients who might otherwise be preparing for surgery, radiation or chemotherapy may now have a different conversation with their doctor.” Today’s approval is for Jemperli used alone in adults with previously untreated stage II or stage III locally advanced rectal cancer. At these stages, the cancer has grown into nearby tissue or reached nearby lymph nodes but has not spread to distant organs. To be eligible, patients’ tumors must be mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H), as determined by an FDA-authorized test. Published estimates suggest that approximately 3% of locally advanced rectal cancers are dMMR or MSI-H. Both terms describe a defect in the way cancer cells correct errors when copying their DNA. Normally, a built-in repair system catches and fixes these mistakes. When the system does not work properly, errors accumulate and create proteins the immune system can recognize, making these tumors particularly vulnerable to immunotherapy. Jemperli works by blocking a signal that cancer cells use to shield themselves from the immune system. Specifically, it targets a protein called PD-1 on immune cells. “Standard treatment for rectal cancer has major life-changing effects. For certain types of rectal cancer, this approval represents a groundbreaking option that avoids surgery, radiation and chemotherapy. This represents a significant benefit for patients and their families,” said Angelo de Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence . “The FDA is acting on emerging evidence to bring new approaches to patients sooner, while requiring further studies to confirm that these treatments provide lasting benefits.” The FDA based its decision on interim results from AZUR-1 ( NCT05723562 ), a phase 2 study evaluating Jemperli alone in 154 patients with previously untreated dMMR or MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer. In the study, patients received up to nine doses of Jemperli, given every 3 weeks over 6 months. After a median follow-up of more than 2 years — meaning at least half of patients had been monitored for that long — almost three-fourths of patients had not needed surgery, radiotherapy or chemotherapy. Longer follow-up is needed to understand the duration of response and how often the cancer returns. An earlier study at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center ( NCT04165772 ) evaluated Jemperli alone in 50 patients with previously untreated dMMR or MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer. None of the patients had detectable signs of cancer after Jemperli treatment, and nearly all patients (93%) maintained that cancer-free status for at least 12 months. Of the 27 patients followed for at least 3 years, only one had their cancer return, and it recurred in the same area. Jemperli can cause the immune system to attack healthy organs and tissues. These reactions can be severe or fatal. The most common side effects, reported in at least 15% of patients treated for this type of rectal cancer, were fatigue, rash, diarrhea and itching. The FDA granted Priority Review to the application and Breakthrough Therapy designation to Jemperli for the treatment of dMMR or MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer. This action marks the 11th approval of a drug reviewed under the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher pilot program , which aims to help accelerate the review of therapies that address national public health priorities. Because this is an accelerated approval based on interim trial results, the sponsor must continue following patients to show these responses create lasting clinical benefit. The approval was granted to GSK. title: Treasury International Capital Data for August 2026
body: October 16, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for August 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for September 2026, is scheduled for November 18, 2026. The sum total in August of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $199.8 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $178.5 billion, and net foreign official inflows were $21.3 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in August; their net purchases were $300.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $257.8 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $42.9 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $21.6 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $279.2 billion in August. Foreign residents decreased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $47.8 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $37.8 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents decreased by $41.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries.
